steps: 1. Open receivables.xlsx -> ooa.excel/open
2. Read the Open Items sheet -> ooa.excel/get_all_cells
3. Close the workbook -> ooa.excel/close
4. Turn the rows into a list of records -> ooa.datatable/to_records
5. Take today's date -> ooa.datetime/now
6. Start the reminder count at 0 -> core/set
7. For each open item -> core/loop
8. Read its due date -> ooa.datetime/parse
9. Count the days past due -> ooa.datetime/difference
10. If it is more than 60 days late -> core/if
11. Email the customer a reminder -> ooa.email/send
12. Count the reminder -> ooa.number/increment
13. Email Meera how many reminders went out -> ooa.email/send
understand: Remind customers whose invoices are more than 60 days past due.

args.body: ${leaver_count} leavers were offboarded.

steps: 1. Read the leavers list -> ooa.csv/read
2. Connect to Active Directory once -> ooa.active_directory/connect
3. Sign in to Okta once -> ooa.okta/connect
4. Sign in to ServiceNow once -> ooa.servicenow/authenticate
5. For each leaver -> core/loop
6. Disable the AD account -> ooa.active_directory/disable_user
7. Remove them from VPN Users -> ooa.active_directory/remove_from_group
8. Move them to Leavers -> ooa.active_directory/move_user
9. Deactivate the Okta user -> ooa.okta/deactivate_user
10. End their Okta sessions -> ooa.okta/clear_sessions
11. Create a ServiceNow incident -> ooa.servicenow/create_record
12. End the ServiceNow session -> ooa.servicenow/end_session
13. Close the Okta session -> ooa.okta/disconnect
14. Disconnect from Active Directory -> ooa.active_directory/disconnect
15. Email HR a summary -> ooa.email/send

flow.name: Expense receipts
flow.description: Read receipt photos, convert amounts to USD and build the claim file.

children.description: Read the text on the receipt
Pick out merchant, date, amount and currency
Add a line to the claim table
Rename the image to merchant and date

steps.description: Email the AP team the claim file with the total

args.subject: Expense claim
args.body: Claim total: ${claim_total} USD from ${receipt_count} receipts.

steps: 1. List the receipt images -> ooa.file/list
2. Start an empty claim table -> ooa.datatable/create_table
3. For each receipt -> core/loop
4. Read the text on the receipt -> ooa.ocr/read_image
5. Pick out merchant, date, amount and currency -> ooa.genai/extract
6. Convert the amount to USD -> ooa.currency/convert
7. Add a line to the claim table -> ooa.datatable/add_row
8. Rename the image to merchant and date -> ooa.file/rename
9. Add up the USD amounts -> ooa.datatable/sum_column
10. Save the claim as claims.csv -> ooa.csv/write
11. Email the AP team the claim file with the total -> ooa.email/send

children.description: Read the text on the receipt
Pick out merchant, date, amount and currency
Add a line to the claim table
Rename the image to merchant and date

steps.description: Email the finance controller the claim file with the total

args.subject: Expense claim
args.body: Claim total: ${claim_total} USD from ${receipt_count} receipts.

steps: 1. List the receipt images -> ooa.file/list
2. Start an empty claim table -> ooa.datatable/create_table
3. For each receipt -> core/loop
4. Read the text on the receipt -> ooa.ocr/read_image
5. Pick out merchant, date, amount and currency -> ooa.genai/extract
6. Convert the amount to USD -> ooa.currency/convert
7. Add a line to the claim table -> ooa.datatable/add_row
8. Rename the image to merchant and date -> ooa.file/rename
9. Add up the USD amounts -> ooa.datatable/sum_column
10. Save the claim as expense_lines.csv -> ooa.csv/write
11. Email the finance controller the claim file with the total -> ooa.email/send
understand: Read receipt photos, convert amounts to USD and build the claim file.

request: Take all the receipt photos (jpg) from D:\Expenses\Receipts, afterwards read each photo with OCR, extract merchant/date/amount/currency, convert to GBP, add it as a line, rename the file date_merchant, and then add up the GBP amounts and write everything to D:\Expenses\claims.csv, and finally email the claim file with the total to the AP team (ap-team@ourfirm.com).
clear: List the .jpg files in D:\Expenses\Receipts, start a claim table; for each receipt: OCR it, extract merchant, date, amount and currency, convert the amount to GBP, add a row and rename the image to date_merchant.jpg, sum the GBP amounts and save the table as D:\Expenses\claims.csv, then email the claim file with the total to ap-team@ourfirm.com.

variables.name: docusign_token
variables.description: DocuSign access token from the vault.

children.description: Send it for signature in DocuSign

steps: 1. Open the tracker -> ooa.excel/open
2. Read the contracts -> ooa.excel/get_all_cells
3. Close the tracker -> ooa.excel/close
4. Keep the ones marked Ready -> ooa.datatable/filter
5. For each ready contract -> core/loop
6. Open the template -> ooa.word/open
7. Fill in the customer name -> ooa.word/replace_text
8. Fill in the contract value -> ooa.word/replace_text
9. Save it as a PDF -> ooa.word/save_as
10. Close the document -> ooa.word/close
11. Send it for signature in DocuSign -> ooa.docusign/create_envelope
12. Log the envelope id -> core/log
understand: Fill the contract template for each ready row and send it out in DocuSign.

request: Read the Contracts sheet of C:\Sales\renewals.xlsx and keep the rows whose Status is Ready, next fill the word template D:\Legal\templates\msa_template.docx per contract (customer + value placeholders), export PDF to C:\Sales\to_sign, then DocuSign it to the row's signer and write the envelope id to the log.
clear: Read the Contracts sheet of C:\Sales\renewals.xlsx and keep the rows with status Ready, then for each ready contract: open D:\Legal\templates\msa_template.docx, fill in customer and value, save it as a PDF in C:\Sales\to_sign, close it, send it for signature in DocuSign to the row's signer and log the envelope id.

variables.name: docusign_token
variables.description: DocuSign access token from the vault.

children.description: Send it for signature in DocuSign

steps: 1. Open the tracker -> ooa.excel/open
2. Read the contracts -> ooa.excel/get_all_cells
3. Close the tracker -> ooa.excel/close
4. Keep the ones marked Ready -> ooa.datatable/filter
5. For each ready contract -> core/loop
6. Open the template -> ooa.word/open
7. Fill in the customer name -> ooa.word/replace_text
8. Fill in the contract value -> ooa.word/replace_text
9. Save it as a PDF -> ooa.word/save_as
10. Close the document -> ooa.word/close
11. Send it for signature in DocuSign -> ooa.docusign/create_envelope
12. Log the envelope id -> core/log
understand: Fill the contract template for each ready row and send it out in DocuSign.

args.text: ${down} of ${server_count} servers did not answer the ping.

steps: 1. Read the server list -> ooa.csv/read
2. Connect to Zendesk once with the saved connection -> ooa.zendesk/connect
3. Start the problem count at 0 -> core/set
4. For each server -> core/loop
5. Ping it -> ooa.network/ping
6. If it does not answer -> core/if
7. Open a Zendesk ticket -> ooa.zendesk/create_ticket
8. Count it -> ooa.number/increment
9. Otherwise: Check the Spooler service -> ooa.services/get_status
10. If the service is not running -> core/if
11. Start Spooler -> ooa.services/start
12. Disconnect from Zendesk -> ooa.zendesk/disconnect
13. If any server was down -> core/if
14. Post the summary in #ap-alerts -> ooa.slack/post_message

steps: 1. Connect to the ledger database once -> ooa.database/connect

args.sql: SELECT Region, Amount FROM invoices WHERE invoice_date >= DATEADD(month, -1, DATEFROMPARTS(YEAR(GETDATE()), MONTH(GETDATE()), 1)) AND invoice_date < DATEFROMPARTS(YEAR(GETDATE()), MONTH(GETDATE()), 1)

steps: 1. Connect to the sales database once -> ooa.database/connect
2. Read last month's invoices -> ooa.database/query
3. Disconnect from the database -> ooa.database/disconnect
4. Total the amount by Region -> ooa.datatable/aggregate
5. Sort by revenue, largest first -> ooa.datatable/sort
6. Add up the total revenue -> ooa.datatable/sum_column
7. Create the workbook -> ooa.excel/create_workbook
8. Write the summary into it -> ooa.excel/write_table
9. Save the workbook -> ooa.excel/save
10. Close the workbook -> ooa.excel/close
11. Upload close_pack.xlsx to the Google Drive folder Ops Reports -> ooa.google/drive_upload
12. Turn the summary into an HTML table -> ooa.datatable/to_html
13. Email HR the summary -> ooa.email/send

flow.name: PO and GRN match
flow.description: Compare ordered and received quantities and chase the buyers for differences.

variables.name: imap_host
variables.description: Mail server of the mailbox, e.g. outlook.office365.com.

steps.description: Match them on PO and line
Sign in to the mailbox for sending once

children.description: If the difference is more than 1

args.subject: PO ${ln.PONumber} line ${ln.Line}: quantity mismatch
args.body: Ordered ${ln.OrderedQty}, received ${ln.ReceivedQty}. Please check with the supplier.

steps: 1. Read the open POs -> ooa.csv/read
2. Open the goods received file -> ooa.excel/open
3. Read the receipts -> ooa.excel/get_all_cells
4. Close it -> ooa.excel/close
5. Match them on PO and line -> ooa.datatable/join
6. Turn the matches into records -> ooa.datatable/to_records
7. Sign in to the mailbox for sending once -> ooa.email/connect
8. For each matched line -> core/loop
9. Work out the quantity difference -> ooa.number/calculate
10. If the difference is more than 1 -> core/if
11. Email the buyer about it -> ooa.email/send
12. Log the mismatch -> core/log
13. Sign out of the mailbox -> ooa.email/disconnect
understand: Compare ordered and received quantities and chase the buyers for differences.

steps: 1. Sign in to Microsoft 365 once -> ooa.microsoft365/connect
2. Connect to Jira once with the saved connection -> ooa.jira/connect
3. For each unread email in Inbox/Customers -> core/loop
4. Find its language -> ooa.genai/detect_language
5. Keep the original text -> core/set
6. If it is not in English -> core/if
7. Translate it to English -> ooa.genai/translate
8. Classify it -> ooa.genai/classify
9. If it is about billing -> core/if
10. Forward it to accounts-receivable@ourfirm.com -> ooa.microsoft365/forward_mail
11. Otherwise: Create a Jira Bug in SUP -> ooa.jira/create_issue
12. Mark it read -> ooa.microsoft365/mark_mail
13. Disconnect from Jira -> ooa.jira/disconnect
14. Sign out of Microsoft 365 -> ooa.microsoft365/disconnect

flow.name: Send payment file to bank

variables.name: m365_token
variables.description: Microsoft Graph access token from the vault.

steps.description: Connect to the ERP database once

args.sql: SELECT * FROM payments WHERE status = 'APPROVED' AND pay_date = TRUNC(SYSDATE)

children.description: Encrypt the file with the bank's PGP key
Take the SHA-256 of the encrypted file
Connect to the bank's SFTP server
Email the treasury team the count and the hash from Outlook 365

else.description: Log that there was nothing to pay

steps: 1. Connect to the ERP database once -> ooa.database/connect

6. Take the SHA-256 of the encrypted file -> ooa.crypto/hash_file
7. Connect to the bank's SFTP server -> ooa.file_transfer/connect
8. Upload it to /inbound -> ooa.file_transfer/upload
9. Disconnect from the server -> ooa.file_transfer/disconnect
10. Email the treasury team the count and the hash from Outlook 365 -> ooa.microsoft365/send_mail
11. Otherwise: Log that there was nothing to pay -> core/log

variables.name: uploader_email
variables.description: Email address of whoever uploads the file.

steps.description: If some rows have no email

args.subject: Upload rejected: rows without email
args.body: ${error_count} rows have no email. See errors.csv.

else.description: Connect to the CRM database once

steps: 1. Wait for the upload -> ooa.file/wait_for_file
2. Read it -> ooa.csv/read
3. Drop empty rows -> ooa.datatable/remove_empty_rows
4. Drop duplicate rows -> ooa.datatable/remove_duplicates
5. Find rows without an email -> ooa.datatable/filter
6. If some rows have no email -> core/if
7. Save them as errors.csv -> ooa.csv/write
8. Email the uploader the errors -> ooa.email/send
9. Otherwise: Connect to the CRM database once -> ooa.database/connect
10. Load the rows into stg_leads -> ooa.database/bulk_insert
11. Disconnect from the database -> ooa.database/disconnect
12. Move the file to C:\Inbound\Done -> ooa.file/move
understand: Check the uploaded CSV and load the clean rows into stg_leads.

request: Wait until D:\Uploads\customers_new.csv lands. Then load it, clean out blank + duplicate lines, then filter rows where Email is empty. Finally bad rows -> errors.csv + mail to the uploader; all good -> load into staging_customers (CRM DB) and move the CSV to C:\Inbound\Done.
clear: Wait for D:\Uploads\customers_new.csv, read it, drop empty and duplicate rows and find the rows without an email, then if any: save them to D:\Uploads\errors.csv and email the uploader; else load the rows into staging_customers and move the file to C:\Inbound\Done.

flow.name: SLA breach watch
flow.description: Escalate open Zendesk tickets older than 48 hours.

variables.name: m365_token
variables.description: Microsoft Graph access token from the vault.

steps.description: Connect to Zendesk once with the saved connection

children.description: Work out its age in hours
If it is older than 48 hours
Post the summary in the IT Teams channel Alerts

steps: 1. Connect to Zendesk once with the saved connection -> ooa.zendesk/connect
2. Find the open tickets -> ooa.zendesk/search_tickets
3. Turn them into records -> ooa.datatable/to_records
4. Take the time now -> ooa.datetime/now
5. For each ticket -> core/loop
6. Read when it was created -> ooa.datetime/parse
7. Work out its age in hours -> ooa.datetime/difference
8. If it is older than 48 hours -> core/if
9. Raise it to urgent -> ooa.zendesk/update_ticket
10. Post the summary in the IT Teams channel Alerts -> ooa.microsoft365/teams_message
11. Disconnect from Zendesk -> ooa.zendesk/disconnect
understand: Escalate open Zendesk tickets older than 48 hours.

flow.name: Stock reorder
flow.description: Order stock that is below its reorder level from the supplier API.

variables.name: supplier_token
variables.description: Supplier API token from the vault.

variables.name: slack_token
variables.description: Slack bot token from the vault.

steps.description: Connect to the inventory database once
Find items below their reorder level

args.sql: SELECT sku, name, qty_on_hand, reorder_level, reorder_qty FROM stock WHERE qty_on_hand < reorder_level

children.description: Place the order with the supplier API

args.sql: UPDATE stock SET on_order = 1 WHERE sku = @sku

children.description: Log the error and go on

args.message: Could not reach the supplier for ${item.sku}.

steps.description: Post how many items were low in #ap-alerts

args.text: ${low_count} items were below their reorder level.

steps: 1. Connect to the inventory database once -> ooa.database/connect
2. Find items below their reorder level -> ooa.database/query
3. For each low item -> core/loop
4. Try to order it -> core/try
5. Place the order with the supplier API -> ooa.rest/request
6. If the order was accepted -> core/if
7. Mark it as ordered -> ooa.database/execute
8. Otherwise: Log the failed order -> core/log
9. On error: Log the error and go on -> core/log
10. Disconnect from the database -> ooa.database/disconnect
11. Post how many items were low in #ap-alerts -> ooa.slack/post_message
understand: Order stock that is below its reorder level from the supplier API.

request: First query stock where qty_on_hand < reorder_level. Next for each one POST an order (sku, reorder_qty) to https://b2b.example-parts.com/api/po; if it comes back 201 set on_order = 1 for it, otherwise log an error. Finally post how many items were low in #ap-alerts on Slack.
clear: Find the stock items below their reorder level, for each: POST the order to https://b2b.example-parts.com/api/po, if 201 mark it on order in the database, else log an error; disconnect, then post how many items were low in the Slack channel #ap-alerts.

args.subject: Access review: Domain Admins
args.body: ${member_count} members; stale accounts are marked.

steps: 1. Connect to Active Directory once -> ooa.active_directory/connect
2. Find the members of Domain Admins -> ooa.active_directory/search
3. Disconnect from Active Directory -> ooa.active_directory/disconnect
4. Take today's date -> ooa.datetime/now
5. Go back 90 days -> ooa.datetime/subtract
6. Add a Stale column -> ooa.datatable/insert_column
7. For each member -> core/loop
8. Read the last logon -> ooa.datetime/parse
9. If it is older than 90 days -> core/if
10. Mark the row stale -> ooa.datatable/set_value
11. Create the review workbook -> ooa.excel/create_workbook
12. Write the members into it -> ooa.excel/write_table
13. Save and close it -> ooa.excel/close
14. Upload review_q3.xlsx to the Finance SharePoint site -> ooa.microsoft365/upload_file
15. Email the security team the review -> ooa.email/send
understand: List the members of Domain Admins, flag stale accounts and send the review out.

flow.description: Remind everyone who has not filled in their hours this week.

variables.description: Google Sheet id of the timesheet.

variables.description: Google access token from the vault.

4. Keep the people with no hours -> ooa.datatable/filter
5. List their emails -> ooa.datatable/column_to_list
6. Sign in to the mailbox once -> ooa.email/connect
7. For each person -> core/loop
8. Email them a reminder -> ooa.email/send
9. Sign out of the mailbox -> ooa.email/disconnect
10. Email the finance controller how many were reminded -> ooa.email/send

flow.name: Deals closing this week
flow.description: Report big deals closing this week and nudge their owners.

variables.name: sf_client_id
variables.description: Consumer key of the Salesforce connected app.

variables.name: sf_client_secret
variables.description: Consumer secret of the connected app, from the vault.

variables.name: m365_token
variables.description: Microsoft Graph access token from the vault.

steps.description: Find open deals closing this week

args.soql: SELECT Id, Name, Amount, CloseDate, Owner.Email, StageName FROM Opportunity WHERE IsClosed = false AND CloseDate = THIS_WEEK

steps.description: Upload closing_this_week.csv to the Finance SharePoint site

args.subject: ${d.Name} closes ${d.CloseDate}
args.body: Your deal ${d.Name} (${d.Amount}) is due to close this week. Any blockers?

steps.description: Post how many big deals close in the HR Teams channel Onboarding

args.message: ${big_count} deals over the limit close this week.

steps: 1. Sign in to Salesforce once -> ooa.salesforce/authenticate
2. Find open deals closing this week -> ooa.salesforce/query
3. End the Salesforce session -> ooa.salesforce/end_session
4. Keep the ones over 250,000 -> ooa.datatable/filter
5. Sort by amount -> ooa.datatable/sort
6. Save them as a CSV -> ooa.csv/write
7. Upload closing_this_week.csv to the Finance SharePoint site -> ooa.microsoft365/upload_file
8. For each big deal -> core/loop
9. Email the owner a nudge -> ooa.email/send
10. Post how many big deals close in the HR Teams channel Onboarding -> ooa.microsoft365/teams_message
understand: Report big deals closing this week and nudge their owners.

else.description: Write the hash next to it

args.subject: Backup check
args.body: Backup check for \\backupsrv\sql\crm_full.bak finished.

steps: 1. Sign in to ServiceNow once -> ooa.servicenow/authenticate
2. If the backup file exists -> core/if
3. Read its details -> ooa.file/get_info
4. Take the time now -> ooa.datetime/now
5. Work out its age in hours -> ooa.datetime/difference
6. Work out its size in MB -> ooa.number/calculate
7. If it is older than a day or under 500 MB -> core/if
8. Create a ServiceNow incident -> ooa.servicenow/create_record
9. Otherwise: Take its SHA-256 -> ooa.crypto/hash_file
10. Write the hash next to it -> ooa.file/write_text
11. Otherwise: Create a ServiceNow incident -> ooa.servicenow/create_record
12. End the ServiceNow session -> ooa.servicenow/end_session
13. Email the IT manager that the check ran -> ooa.email/send
understand: Check that last night's backup exists, is recent and big enough.

steps: 1. Sign in to ServiceNow once -> ooa.servicenow/authenticate
2. If the backup file exists -> core/if
3. Read its details -> ooa.file/get_info
4. Take the time now -> ooa.datetime/now
5. Work out its age in hours -> ooa.datetime/difference
6. Work out its size in MB -> ooa.number/calculate
7. If it is older than a day or under 1000 MB -> core/if
8. Create a ServiceNow incident -> ooa.servicenow/create_record
9. Otherwise: Take its SHA-256 -> ooa.crypto/hash_file
10. Write the hash next to it -> ooa.file/write_text
11. Otherwise: Create a ServiceNow incident -> ooa.servicenow/create_record
12. End the ServiceNow session -> ooa.servicenow/end_session
13. Email the IT manager that the check ran -> ooa.email/send

flow.name: Schedule interviews
flow.description: Book an interview for each shortlisted candidate and tell them.

variables.name: m365_token
variables.description: Microsoft Graph access token from the vault.

children.description: Add one hour for the end

args.subject: Your interview with OurFirm
args.body: Hi ${c.Name}, your interview is on ${c.Slot}. The invite is in your calendar.

steps.description: Post how many were booked in the Sales Teams channel Pipeline

steps: 1. Open the shortlist -> ooa.excel/open
2. Read the candidates -> ooa.excel/get_all_cells
3. Close the shortlist -> ooa.excel/close
4. Sign in to Microsoft 365 once -> ooa.microsoft365/connect
5. For each candidate -> core/loop
6. Read the slot -> ooa.datetime/parse
7. Add one hour for the end -> ooa.datetime/add
8. Book the interview in Outlook -> ooa.microsoft365/create_event
9. Email the candidate the details -> ooa.microsoft365/send_mail
10. Sign out of Microsoft 365 -> ooa.microsoft365/disconnect
11. Post how many were booked in the Sales Teams channel Pipeline -> ooa.microsoft365/teams_message
understand: Book an interview for each shortlisted candidate and tell them.

flow.name: Monthly invoices
flow.description: Create a tax invoice PDF per customer with 5% tax and send it.

variables.name: imap_host
variables.description: Mail server of the mailbox, e.g. outlook.office365.com.

steps.description: Connect to the billing database once

args.sql: SELECT customer, email, SUM(amount) AS net FROM usage WHERE month = date_trunc('month', now()) GROUP BY customer, email

steps.description: Sign in to the billing mailbox once

children.description: Email the invoice to the customer

args.subject: Your invoice
args.body: Please find your invoice attached. Total due: ${gross}.

steps: 1. Connect to the billing database once -> ooa.database/connect
2. Read this month's billable usage -> ooa.database/query
3. Disconnect from the database -> ooa.database/disconnect
4. Sign in to the billing mailbox once -> ooa.email/connect
5. For each customer -> core/loop
6. Work out the 5% tax -> ooa.number/calculate
7. Work out the gross total -> ooa.number/calculate
8. Open the invoice template -> ooa.word/open
9. Fill in the customer -> ooa.word/replace_text
10. Fill in the net amount -> ooa.word/replace_text
11. Fill in the tax -> ooa.word/replace_text
12. Fill in the total -> ooa.word/replace_text
13. Save it as a PDF -> ooa.word/save_as
14. Close the document -> ooa.word/close
15. Email the invoice to the customer -> ooa.email/send
16. Sign out of the mailbox -> ooa.email/disconnect
understand: Create a tax invoice PDF per customer with 5% tax and send it.

variables.description: Mail server of the mailbox, e.g. outlook.office365.com.

steps.description: Connect to the billing database once

args.sql: SELECT customer, email, SUM(amount) AS net FROM usage WHERE month = date_trunc('month', now()) GROUP BY customer, email

steps.description: Sign in to the billing mailbox once

children.description: Email the invoice to the customer

args.subject: Your invoice
args.body: Please find your invoice attached. Total due: ${gross}.

steps: 1. Connect to the billing database once -> ooa.database/connect
2. Read this month's billable usage -> ooa.database/query
3. Disconnect from the database -> ooa.database/disconnect
4. Sign in to the billing mailbox once -> ooa.email/connect
5. For each customer -> core/loop
6. Work out the 5% tax -> ooa.number/calculate
7. Work out the gross total -> ooa.number/calculate
8. Open the invoice template -> ooa.word/open
9. Fill in the customer -> ooa.word/replace_text
10. Fill in the net amount -> ooa.word/replace_text
11. Fill in the tax -> ooa.word/replace_text
12. Fill in the total -> ooa.word/replace_text
13. Save it as a PDF -> ooa.word/save_as
14. Close the document -> ooa.word/close
15. Email the invoice to the customer -> ooa.email/send
16. Sign out of the mailbox -> ooa.email/disconnect
understand: Create a tax invoice PDF per customer with 5% tax and send it.

request: Sum this month's usage by customer (billing DB), then for each customer work out 12% tax and the gross, fill D:\Billing\invoice_template.docx (customer, net, tax, total), save it as a PDF in D:\Billing\Invoices and email it to the customer.
clear: Read this month's billable amount per customer from the billing database, then for each customer: compute 12% tax and the gross, fill D:\Billing\invoice_template.docx, save it as a PDF in D:\Billing\Invoices and email it to the customer.

flow.name: Book supplier credit notes
flow.description: Read emailed credit notes, book the ones that match an invoice and ask about the rest.

variables.name: imap_host
variables.description: Mail server of the mailbox, e.g. outlook.office365.com.

steps.description: Sign in to the AP mailbox once
Connect to the AP database once
For each unread email in AP/Credits

children.description: Pick out credit note number, original invoice and amount

args.sql: SELECT id FROM ap_invoices WHERE invoice_no = @inv
INSERT INTO ap_credits (credit_note, invoice_no, amount) VALUES (@cn, @inv, @amt)

else.description: Ask the supplier for the invoice reference

args.body: We could not match credit note ${cn.credit_note} to an invoice. Which invoice does it credit?

steps: 1. Sign in to the AP mailbox once -> ooa.email/connect
2. Connect to the AP database once -> ooa.database/connect
3. For each unread email in AP/Credits -> core/loop
4. Save the PDFs to D:\AP\Credits\New -> ooa.email/save_attachments
5. For each credit note -> core/loop
6. Read the credit note -> ooa.pdf/extract_text
7. Pick out credit note number, original invoice and amount -> ooa.genai/extract
8. Look up the original invoice -> ooa.database/query
9. If the invoice is found -> core/if
10. Book the credit against it -> ooa.database/execute
11. File it in D:\AP\Credits\Booked -> ooa.file/move
12. Otherwise: Ask the supplier for the invoice reference -> ooa.email/reply
13. Mark the email read -> ooa.email/mark
14. Disconnect from the database -> ooa.database/disconnect
15. Sign out of the mailbox -> ooa.email/disconnect
understand: Read emailed credit notes, book the ones that match an invoice and ask about the rest.

flow.description: Apply the bank's receipts file to open invoices and report what did not match.

variables.description: Microsoft Graph access token from the vault.

steps.description: Connect to the bank's SFTP server
Start a table of unmatched receipts
Connect to the receivables database once

args.sql: UPDATE ar_invoices SET status = 'paid', paid_on = CURRENT_DATE WHERE invoice_no = @ref AND amount = @amt

children.description: Add it to the unmatched table

steps.description: If some receipts did not match

children.description: Email the treasury team the summary from Outlook 365

args.subject: Unapplied cash
args.body: ${open_count} receipts could not be applied.

steps: 1. Connect to the bank's SFTP server -> ooa.file_transfer/connect
2. Download daily_receipts.csv -> ooa.file_transfer/download
3. Disconnect from the server -> ooa.file_transfer/disconnect
4. Read the receipts -> ooa.csv/read
5. Start a table of unmatched receipts -> ooa.datatable/create_table
6. Connect to the receivables database once -> ooa.database/connect
7. For each receipt -> core/loop
8. Mark the invoice paid -> ooa.database/execute
9. If no invoice matched -> core/if
10. Add it to the unmatched table -> ooa.datatable/add_row
11. Disconnect from the database -> ooa.database/disconnect
12. Count the unmatched receipts -> ooa.datatable/row_count
13. If some receipts did not match -> core/if
14. Save them as unapplied_cash.csv -> ooa.csv/write
15. Email the treasury team the summary from Outlook 365 -> ooa.microsoft365/send_mail
16. Otherwise: Log a full match -> core/log
understand: Apply the bank's receipts file to open invoices and report what did not match.

flow.name: Slack helpdesk triage
flow.description: Classify the last hour of #it-helpdesk with AI and open tickets for hardware problems.

variables.name: slack_token
variables.description: Slack bot token from the vault.

steps.description: Connect to Jira once with the saved connection

children.description: Ask the AI what kind of request it is
If it is a hardware problem
Create a Jira Bug in SUP
Answer in the thread with the ticket

else.description: Point them to the self-service portal

steps: 1. Take the time now -> ooa.datetime/now
2. Go back one hour -> ooa.datetime/subtract
3. Read the last hour of #it-helpdesk -> ooa.slack/get_conversation_history
4. Connect to Jira once with the saved connection -> ooa.jira/connect
5. For each message -> core/loop
6. Ask the AI what kind of request it is -> ooa.genai/classify
7. If it is a hardware problem -> core/if

variables.description: Google Sheet id of the dispute log.

args.note: Customer dispute - please hold dunning for this invoice.

steps: 1. Sign in to the AR mailbox once -> ooa.email/connect
2. Start the dispute log rows -> ooa.datatable/create_table
3. For each unread email in AR about an invoice -> core/loop
4. Ask the AI if the customer disputes the invoice -> ooa.genai/classify
5. If it is a dispute -> core/if
6. Forward it to the collections team -> ooa.email/forward
7. Add it to the dispute log rows -> ooa.datatable/add_row
8. Mark it read -> ooa.email/mark
9. Sign out of the mailbox -> ooa.email/disconnect
10. Append the disputes to the Google Sheet -> ooa.google/sheets_append
